items.title: Earth’s oldest trees reveal history’s strongest solar storms
items.description: Although humanity continuously reckons with many problems here on Earth — war, political turmoil, epidemics and pandemics, all while the energy, climate, and water crises intensify — it’s important to remember just how relentless the Universe can be. While earthquakes, tornadoes, volcanoes, hurricanes and other natural disasters haven’t exactly ceased in the meantime, there’s a completely different looming threat for which we’re completely unprepared:  a solar storm . items.title: The case for breaking out of your academic box
items.description:
Alan Love, philosopher and Director of the Minnesota Center for Philosophy of Science at the University of Minnesota, makes the historical case for why academic disciplines exist — and why they’ve outlasted their original purpose.

items.title: Pressure doesn’t create leaders. It reveals what we failed to rehearse.
items.description:
Leadership isn’t defined only by the biggest moments we face. It’s shaped in the moments between them: the first five minutes after a reorganization is announced. How a leader responds when priorities suddenly change. The silence after difficult feedback. 
 These moments rarely make headlines, yet they quietly shape trust, culture, and momentum every single day. They’re where leadership is experienced. Because they carry consequence, nd the weight of those consequences is experienced as pressure

items.title: Terance Tao: Understanding 6 essential mathematical concepts
items.description:
Terence Tao has spent decades solving problems most people can’t even state, and he says he’s never had a single eureka moment. In this conversation, the UCLA mathematician and Fields Medalist breaks math down to six essential ideas: numbers, algebra, geometry, probability, analysis, and dynamics. 
 
 This video  Terance Tao: Understanding 6 essential mathematical concepts  is featured on  Big Think .

items.title: For women and children in West Africa, medical treatment often came too late. Then one model changed where care begins.
items.description:
In 2009, a community health worker in the bustling capital of Bamako, Mali, found a young boy at home who had become dangerously ill within a matter of hours. Recognizing he needed urgent medical care, she arranged for him to be taken to a health facility.

items.title: Flying clocks in opposite directions around the world proved Einstein right

items.title: Cosmic birefringence: the signal that could upend cosmology
items.description: One of the most enduring principles in the entire Universe is the cosmological principle: an outgrowth of the Copernican revolution.
